title: TLS Certificate analysis: Google Trust Services, ECDSA 256, and isolated SAN
summary: Nmap's ssl-cert script inspected the TLS certificate for www.radblok.co.za. The certificate is issued by Google Trust Services (WE1 CA) using modern 256-bit Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECDSA) with a 90-day automated ACME lifecycle (Sept 20 to Dec 19, 2026). The Subject Alternative Name (SAN) contains only DNS:www.radblok.co.za, indicating isolated single-domain certificate issuance rather than a shared wildcard.

rows: Google Trust Services is an automated ACME Certificate Authority. Cloudflare and Render integrate GTS alongside Let's Encrypt for automatic TLS provisioning.

Modern Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC / prime256v1). ECDSA provides equivalent security to RSA 3072-bit with substantially smaller key sizes, lower CPU overhead, and faster TLS handshakes on mobile devices.

**No Wildcards or Leaked Staging Subdomains**. The certificate covers strictly `www.radblok.co.za`. It does not include `radblok.co.za` or any internal/dev hostnames in this specific cert, showing targeted per-hostname provisioning.
Standard 90-day automated lifecycle. Issued recently on September 20, managed via automated background renewal.
Adds a third ingress IP in the `216.24.57.0/24` subnet alongside the `.16` and `.18` addresses discovered in Entry 011.

sections.h: Why SAN inspection matters in recon

blocks.text: In security assessments, inspecting the Subject Alternative Name (SAN) field is a key technique for discovering hidden attack surfaces. Multi-domain certificates or wildcards often bundle related hostnames together, such as `admin.target.com`, `vpn.target.com`, or `dev-backend.target.com`.
Here, Render/Cloudflare requested a tightly scoped single-name certificate solely for `www.radblok.co.za`, leaving no ancillary hostnames exposed in the SAN.

items: TLS profile completed: ECDSA 256-bit issued by Google Trust Services (WE1).
